memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Even the priests, who approach the LORD, must consecrate themselves, or the
LORD will break out against them.' Moses said to the LORD, 'The people cannot
come up Mount Sinai, because you yourself warned us, "Put limits around the
mountain and set it apart as holy."'" - Ex 19:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Even the priests." Those whose whole role was to approach God still had to
consecrate themselves.

There is no professional exemption from holiness. Familiarity with sacred things
does not make a person safe around them. If anything, the danger increases,
because routine dulls reverence.

This is a word for anyone who serves. Pastors, teachers, worship leaders, Sunday
school helpers, anyone who handles holy things regularly. The person who prepares
the sermon can stop hearing it. The one who leads the songs can stop singing
them.

Paul, after all his ministry, wrote about disciplining himself so that "after I
have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified" (1 Cor 9:27). He did
not consider his position a guarantee.

Notice Moses' reply. He tells God the people cannot come up because God Himself
set the limits. It reads almost like Moses gently reminding God of His own
instructions. God does not rebuke him for it. There is a striking freedom in
Moses' speech with God.

Nevertheless, God repeats the warning in the next verse. Sometimes we need to
hear a thing twice.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has serving God made you less attentive to God?
2. Where has routine dulled your reverence?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, keep me from handling holy things carelessly. Let familiarity never replace
reverence. Amen.
